EOSE.business: Zinc-based long-duration energy storage; the key business question is whether production growth can become profitable deliveries.
EOSE.bull_case: Revenue and manufacturing scale are improving. Continued shipment growth and margin improvement could strengthen the operating thesis.
EOSE.bear_case: Gross margins remain deeply negative. Production ramp, financing, dilution, and conversion of backlog to cash remain important risks.

notes.title: Preliminary Q3 update: growth with continuing losses at gross-margin level
notes.fact: Eos estimated Q3 revenue of $82–83 million and GAAP gross margin of −55% to −53%. It expected annual revenue in the lower half of its $300–350 million range. These figures are preliminary.
notes.interpretation: Growth supports the manufacturing-ramp thesis, while negative gross margins and the lower-half revenue outlook temper it. This does not predict a price rise.

events.title: Q3 results before US market open; conference call at 08:30 New York time

ONDS.business: Autonomous defense, drones, robotics and related technologies; monitor whether orders convert into deliveries and sustainable operating earnings.
ONDS.bull_case: New orders and a broader defense portfolio support the demand thesis. Delivery milestones and conversion of backlog into revenue are the key evidence to watch.
ONDS.bear_case: Acquisition integration, cash deployment, dilution, delivery timing and continuing operating losses can offset strong order headlines.

notes.title: Order update: more than $165 million of additional orders
notes.fact: Ondas reported over $165 million in orders in the second half of August through October 1, bringing disclosed orders since June 30 above $270 million.
notes.interpretation: Orders support demand visibility, but they are not the same as revenue, cash collected or profit. The announcement alone does not establish a two-week catalyst.

notes.title: Q2 operating baseline
notes.fact: Ondas reported Q2 revenue of $83.8 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $50.6 million. Adjusted EBITDA is a company-defined non-GAAP measure.
notes.interpretation: The investment thesis depends on future delivery and operating leverage, not revenue growth alone. This quarterly baseline is older than the current news review.
